title: First written mention of Lithuania
place: Quedlinburg, Germany (where the annals were written)
description: The Annals of Quedlinburg record that the missionary Bruno of Querfurt was killed on the border of Rus' and Lithuania, the first known use of the country's name.

title: Battle of Saule
description: Samogitians and Semigallians defeat the Livonian Brothers of the Sword, whose remnants are merged into the Teutonic Order.

title: Mindaugas crowned king
description: Mindaugas, who had united the Lithuanian lands and accepted baptism, is crowned with the pope's approval, the only crowned king of Lithuania.

title: Battle of Durbe
description: Samogitians rout the combined forces of the Teutonic and Livonian orders, setting off revolts among the conquered Baltic peoples.

title: Vilnius first named in the letters of Gediminas
description: Grand Duke Gediminas writes from Vilnius inviting German merchants and craftsmen to settle, the first written record of the city.

title: Christianisation of Lithuania
description: Jogaila, now king of Poland, returns to Vilnius to begin the baptism of the Lithuanians into the Latin church, and a cathedral and bishopric are founded.

title: Treaty of Melno
description: The Teutonic Order gives up its claim to Samogitia, fixing a border with Prussia that stays unchanged for about five hundred years.

title: Death of Vytautas the Great
description: The grand duke under whom Lithuania reached its greatest extent dies while waiting for a royal crown sent by Emperor Sigismund.

title: Battle of Orsha
description: A Lithuanian and Polish army under Konstanty Ostrogski defeats a larger Muscovite force, slowing Moscow's advance after the loss of Smolensk.

title: First Statute of Lithuania
description: The Grand Duchy adopts a written code of law for the whole state, revised in 1566 and 1588 and in use until 1840.

title: First Lithuanian book printed
description: The Lutheran catechism of Martynas Mažvydas is printed in Königsberg, the first printed book in the Lithuanian language.

title: Vilnius University founded
description: King Stephen Báthory raises the Jesuit college of Vilnius to a university, the oldest in the Baltic states.

title: Russian army takes Vilnius
description: The army of Tsar Alexis captures, plunders and burns Vilnius, the first time the capital falls to a foreign power.

title: Union of Kėdainiai
description: With the country overrun by Russian and Swedish armies, the Radziwiłłs and other magnates sign a union with Sweden in place of that with Poland, which lapses within two years.

title: Napoleon crosses the Nemunas
description: The Grande Armée crosses the river at Kaunas to begin the invasion of Russia and re-crosses it in December with a fraction of its men.

title: Vilnius University closed
description: Tsar Nicholas I closes the university after the uprising of 1830 to 1831, leaving Lithuania without a university until the twentieth century.

title: Lithuanian press ban
description: After the January Uprising the Russian authorities forbid printing Lithuanian in Latin letters, and for forty years books are smuggled in from East Prussia.

title: Aušra first published
description: The first national Lithuanian newspaper is printed in East Prussia and smuggled across the border, a milestone of the national revival.

title: Great Seimas of Vilnius
description: About two thousand delegates meet during the Russian revolution and demand autonomy for Lithuania within its ethnic borders.

title: Act of Independence
description: The Council of Lithuania declares the restoration of an independent state with Vilnius as its capital.

title: Żeligowski's Mutiny
description: Polish troops under General Lucjan Żeligowski seize Vilnius in a staged mutiny, and the city stays in Poland until 1939 while Kaunas serves as Lithuania's capital.

title: Klaipėda Revolt
description: Lithuanian volunteers take the Klaipėda (Memel) region from its French administrators, giving the country its only seaport.

title: Coup of December 1926
description: Army officers overthrow the elected government and install Antanas Smetona, who rules as an authoritarian president until 1940.

title: Germany takes Klaipėda
description: Lithuania yields to a German ultimatum and hands over the Klaipėda region, Germany's last territorial gain before the war.

title: Soviet occupation
description: The Red Army occupies Lithuania after an ultimatum, and a staged election and annexation by the Soviet Union follow in August.

title: Ponary massacre
description: German units and Lithuanian collaborators shoot up to 100,000 people, most of them Jews of Vilnius, in the forest at Paneriai.

title: Partisans' declaration of 16 February
description: The leaders of the armed resistance to Soviet rule meet in a bunker and declare their council the lawful authority of Lithuania.

title: Self-immolation of Romas Kalanta
description: A nineteen-year-old sets himself on fire in protest against Soviet rule, and his funeral sets off two days of demonstrations.

title: Baltic Way
description: About two million people join hands in a chain from Vilnius through Riga to Tallinn on the fiftieth anniversary of the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact.

title: Independence restored
description: The newly elected Supreme Council declares the re-establishment of the state, making Lithuania the first Soviet republic to declare independence.

title: January Events
description: Soviet troops storm the television tower and broadcasting centre, killing fourteen unarmed civilians, but do not attack the parliament defended by crowds.

title: Lithuania joins the European Union
description: Lithuania becomes a member of the European Union, a month after joining NATO.
